== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' married [[Allan-6611|Rose Allan]] in 1769, according to a family chronology transcribing the register of the Old Kilwaughter/Larne Non-Subscribing Presbyterian Church ("HOTT" church) in Larne, County Antrim.<ref name="Timeline">Donna Jean Glasgow, [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html "GLASGOWS from Kilwaughter Parish and Larne, County Antrim, Northern Ireland … Timeline"] (archived 24 November 2010), a transcription of the Old Kilwaughter/Larne Non-Subscribing Presbyterian register entries. The chronology records "John3 Glasgow m. Rose Allan in 1769, born perhaps 1745–48", and distinguishes him from John2, master of the ship ''Abigail'', in 1739; the "born perhaps 1745–48" is the chronology's own estimate, not a baptism.</ref>

The chronology gives only the marriage year, so John's birth is set to about 1747, and Larne is inferred from the marriage.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1499]] is assessed at 48% (possible). John’s established Larne family, c 1747 generation and association with the local trades network fit Hugh-1499 and his proved son James born c 1748. A brother placement is a coherent reconstruction of the close local family, but the monument and held deeds name no John as Hugh’s son.

Possible 48%; locality, generation and associates, without a named-son clause. Ann is not inferred as mother.

Next useful test: Test John and James together in the Larne deeds and family property.

Source basis already held: [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html Donna Jean Glasgow, "GLASGOWS from Kilwaughter Parish and Larne, County Antrim, Northern Ireland … Timeline" () (archived 24 November 2010), a transcription of the Old Kilwaughter/Larne Non-Subscribing Presbyterian register entries]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.


'''Uncertain father.''' [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]] is a tentative father, with low confidence. Hugh's Larne household and approximate age are compatible with a son born about 1747, but no identified record calls John his son. The attachment is a working hypothesis, not a proved descent. John's mother remains unidentified; Hugh's wife Ann cannot be assumed to be his mother. The chronology's birth range is an estimate, not a baptism.<ref name="Timeline" />

The evidence does not establish the proposed relationship:

* The Glasgow memorial stone at Larne names Hugh Glasgow (d. 8 Jul 1767 aged 62), his wife Ann (d. 8 Jun 1786 aged 75), a young Hugh (d. 30 Nov 1756 aged 11), their son James (d. 14 Apr 1812 aged 64), James's wife Jane and their daughter Ann — no John.<ref>''Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim'' (Ulster Journal of Archaeology), [https://archive.org/stream/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala_djvu.txt Glasgow stone at Larne], pp. 47–48.</ref>
* The register chronology lists Hugh's children as Jean (1731), Rose (1735), Mary (1736), James (1737), Hugh (1745) and James (1747/48) — no John.
* The Registry of Deeds memorials for the Larne/Kilwaughter Glasgows name Robert of Kilwaughter (1738/1741), William of Larne (1736/1737) and James the ropemaker (1766/1775), but these cited entries do not identify this John or his father.<ref>Registry of Deeds Index Project, [https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/mem.php?memorial=74015 memorial 74015], [https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/mem.php?memorial=62131 62131], [https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/mem.php?memorial=67416 67416], [https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/mem.php?memorial=204122 204122].</ref>
* Classon Porter's congregational memoir (session book) names Hugh, James and Robert only.<ref>Classon Porter, [https://archive.org/stream/christianunitari0003unse/christianunitari0003unse_djvu.txt ''Congregational Memoirs — Larne and Kilwaughter''], The Christian Unitarian 3 (1864).</ref>

Hugh is the leading working candidate because his documented Larne family fits the place and generation. The elder [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] remains a plausible alternative. John's absence from the memorial and derivative baptism list is a caution, not proof that he was unrelated: neither has been established as a complete list of surviving children. The shipmaster John mentioned in the chronology is not independently identified as his father.

The original congregational registers (PRONI MIC/1B/6, baptisms 1720–1769 and marriages 1721–1769) and the renewal endorsements to the 1736 Larne lease (PRONI D2977/3A/4/81/72A) may help distinguish the candidates. These records require further inspection; none is claimed here to name John's father.

'''Same-name Scottish child.''' [[Glasgow-2846|John Glasgow of West Calder]], son of [[Glasgow-2847|John Glasgow]] and [[Anderson-83671|Margaret Anderson]], has a separate Scottish baptism citation. The Larne marriage chronology does not identify its groom as that child. The two men are kept separate unless evidence connects them.

A possible identification concerns John Glasco, charged at Bow Street. John Glasco, Esq., said he was an officer on the Staff and was brought before the Bow Street magistrate charged with wounding patrolman John Smith. The reported incident occurred on Tuesday night after the play in Covent Garden; Glasco was committed.<ref>The Times, 2 May 1799, p.3, Public Office, Bow Street; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/32820363/ record].</ref> Allegation and committal are not conviction. Military status is self-reported and unconfirmed; no Irish origin or kin is stated. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns John Glascow, London chairman. John Glascow, a chairman, said he saw a man in black running with pistols after Martha Ray was shot in Covent Garden.<ref>Derby Mercury, provider-labelled 19 March 1779, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/394231375/ record]; Old Bailey original, printed p.207; [https://www.dhi.ac.uk/san/ob/1770s/177904040005.gif record]; Old Bailey Proceedings, James Hackman record t17790404-3; event dating only; [https://www.oldbaileyonline.org/record/t17790404-3 record].</ref> The Old Bailey indictment specifies that Martha Ray was shot on 7 April 1779 (printed p.207); that is the event date, not the indictment or newspaper publication date. The newspaper describes evidence after the shooting, not established trial testimony. Its March provider label is incorrect. The identification remains uncertain.
